q: What circumstances are the believers enduring in Thessalonica?
a: The believers are enduring persecutions and afflictions.

q: What will be the positive result of the circumstances the believers are enduring?
a: The believers will be counted worthy of the kingdom of God.

q: What will God do to those who afflict the believers?
a: God will afflict those who afflict the believers, punishing them with flaming fire.

q: When will the believers be relieved of their afflictions?
a: The believers will be relieved when Jesus Christ is revealed from heaven.

q: How long will the punishment be for those who do not know God?
a: The punishment for those who do not know God will be eternal.

q: From what are those who do not know God separated as part of their punishment?
a: Those who do not know God are separated from the presence of the Lord as part of their punishment.

q: What will the believers do when they see Christ come on his day?
a: The believers will marvel at Christ when he comes on his day.

q: About what event does Paul say he is now going to write?
a: Paul says he is now going to write concerning the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ.

q: What does Paul tell them not to believe?
a: Paul tells them not to believe that the day of the Lord has already come.

q: What does Paul say must come before the day of the Lord?
a: The falling away and the revealing of the man of lawlessness must come before the day of the Lord.

q: What does the man of lawlessness do?
a: The man of lawlessness opposes and exalts himself against God, sitting in the temple of God and portraying himself as God.

q: When will the man of lawlessness be revealed?
a: The man of lawlessness will be revealed when it is time, when the one who restrains him is taken out of the way.

q: What will Jesus do to the man of lawlessness when Jesus is revealed?
a: When Jesus is revealed, he will kill the man of lawlessness.

q: Who is working with the man of lawlessness to give him power, signs, and false wonders?
a: Satan is working with the man of lawlessness to give him power, signs, and false wonders.

q: In what do those who are deceived and perishing take pleasure?
a: Those who are deceived and perishing take pleasure in unrighteousness.

q: What did God choose for the Thessalonians to obtain through the gospel?
a: God chose for the Thessalonians to obtain the glory of the Lord Jesus Christ through the gospel.

q: What does Paul call the Thessalonians to do now that they have received the gospel?
a: Paul calls the Thessalonians to stand firm and to grasp the traditions that they were taught.

q: In what does Paul desire the Thessalonians to be established in their hearts?
a: Paul desires that the Thessalonians be established in every good work and word.

q: For what does Paul want the Thessalonians to pray regarding the word of the Lord?
a: Paul wants the Thessalonians to pray that the word of the Lord would spread rapidly and be glorified.

q: What does Paul tell the Thessalonians to continue to do?
a: Paul tells the Thessalonians to continue to do the things he has commanded them.

q: How are the believers to react every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the traditions they received from Paul?
a: The believers are to avoid every brother who walks disorderly and not according to the traditions they received from Paul.

q: What example did Paul set for the Thessalonians regarding his work and support?
a: Paul labored night and day, paying for his food, and not being a burden to anyone.

q: What did Paul command concerning anyone who does not want to work?
a: Paul commanded that anyone who does not want to work should not eat.

q: Instead of being lazy, what does Paul command such people to do?
a: Paul commands the lazy to work with quietness and to eat their own food.

q: What are the brothers to do with anyone who does not obey Paul’s instruction in this letter?
a: The brothers are to have no association with anyone who does not obey Paul’s instruction in this letter.

q: What does Paul desire that the Lord would give the Thessalonians?
a: Paul desires that the Lord would give the Thessalonians peace at all times in all ways.

q: How does Paul show that he is the author of this letter?
a: Paul wrote the greeting with his own hand as the sign that he is the author.
